fullPassage:
(A) Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. In addition to a variety of other duties, every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level. The goal was to raise the reading level of the students with whom she worked to help enable her school to ascend from its "academic emergency" status under the state's education rules. Emma was in one of Sandy's afternoon reading groups, and she was not improving. (a) She lacked patience and often lost focus, at which point she became disruptive, primarily to amuse herself, or so it seemed.

(B) That evening after school, Sandy reflected on what Emma had said. Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading to improve her ability to sound out words. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some one-on-one reading instruction in addition to the small-group time. In those one-on-one meetings, Sandy let Emma select a book from a handful of books that were at (b) her reading level. Then Sandy would read a paragraph out loud and have Emma read one.

(C) They would continue to swap back and forth. Slowly but surely, they saw improvement. Over time, they were able to increase the reading level of the books as Emma's ability to sound out words improved. Sandy also noticed that Emma came to reading group with her classmates and started to make it through the entire lesson without becoming disruptive or feeling anxious. More than anything, her newfound confidence made (c) her want to try and read other books!

questions.passage: Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. Every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level. Emma was in one of Sandy's afternoon reading groups, and she was not ①<u>improve</u>. She lacked patience and often ②<u>lost</u> focus, at which point she became ③<u>disruptive</u>, primarily to ④<u>amuse</u> herself.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ②lost(과거형), ③disruptive(형용사), ④amuse(동사원형)는 정상입니다. ①improve는 was not 뒤에 진행형이므로 improving이 올바릅니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① improve → improving: was not improving(과거진행형)
✅ ② lost: 과거 시제
✅ ③ disruptive: became + 형용사
✅ ④ amuse: to amuse(to부정사 목적)
det.tip: was not improving: 과거진행형 부정. improve(원형)가 아닌 improving(-ing)

questions.passage: Sandy recalled research ①<u>suggesting</u> she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading to improve her ability to ②<u>sound</u> out words. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some one-on-one reading instruction. In those meetings, Sandy let Emma ③<u>to select</u> a book from a handful of books. Then Sandy would read a paragraph out loud and have Emma ④<u>read</u> one.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①suggesting(현재분사), ②sound(동사원형), ④read(동사원형)는 정상입니다. ③to select는 사역동사 let 뒤이므로 select(동사원형)가 올바릅니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① suggesting: 현재분사 (research suggesting)
✅ ② sound: ability to V (동사원형)
❌ ③ to select → select: let + O + V(원형)
✅ ④ read: have + O + V(원형)
det.tip: 사역동사 let/have/make + O + V(원형): to부정사가 아닌 원형부정사

questions.passage: They would continue to swap back and forth. Slowly but surely, they saw improvement. Over time, they were able to increase the reading level of the books as Emma's ability ①<u>to sound</u> out words improved. Sandy also noticed that Emma came to reading group and started ②<u>to make</u> it through the entire lesson without ③<u>becoming</u> disruptive or ④<u>feel</u> anxious.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①to sound(to부정사), ②to make(to부정사), ③becoming(동명사)은 정상입니다. ④feel은 without 뒤 becoming과 병렬이므로 feeling(-ing)이 올바릅니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① to sound: ability to V
✅ ② to make: started to V
✅ ③ becoming: without + -ing
❌ ④ feel → feeling: without becoming or feeling 병렬
det.tip: without + -ing: becoming과 feeling이 or로 병렬. 둘 다 동명사

questions.passage: Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. Every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level. The goal was to raise the reading level of the students to help enable her school to ascend from its "academic emergency" status. Emma was in one of Sandy's groups and was not improving.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 원문의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"Sandy는 중학교 교사였고, 6학년 학생들을 가르쳤다."

det.korean: 원문은 초등학교(elementary school) 교사이며 3학년(third graders) 학생들과 일했습니다.
det.analysis: ❌ F: elementary school(초등학교) ≠ 중학교, third graders(3학년) ≠ 6학년
det.tip: 학교급/학년 변조: elementary(초등) vs 중학교, third(3학년) vs 6학년

questions.passage: That evening after school, Sandy reflected on what Emma had said. Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some one-on-one reading instruction in addition to the small-group time.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 원문의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"Sandy는 소그룹 시간을 대신하여 일대일 교육을 진행했다."

det.korean: 원문은 'in addition to the small-group time'으로 소그룹 시간에 추가로 일대일 교육을 한 것입니다. '대신하여'가 아닙니다.
det.analysis: ❌ F: in addition to(추가로) ≠ 대신하여(instead of)
det.tip: in addition to(~에 추가로) ↔ instead of(~대신에): 핵심 전치사 변조

questions.passage: They would continue to swap back and forth. Slowly but surely, they saw improvement. Over time, they were able to increase the reading level of the books. Sandy noticed that Emma started to make it through the entire lesson without becoming disruptive or feeling anxious.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 원문의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"시간이 지나면서 Emma는 수업 전체를 방해 없이 끝까지 마칠 수 있게 되었다."

det.korean: 원문 'started to make it through the entire lesson without becoming disruptive'와 일치합니다.
det.analysis: ✅ T: 수업 전체 참여 + 방해 없음: 원문과 일치
det.tip: make it through = 끝까지 마치다. without becoming disruptive = 방해 없이

questions.passage: Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. Every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level. The goal was to raise the reading level of the students to help enable her school to ascend from its "academic emergency" status. Emma was in one of Sandy's groups and was not improving. She lacked patience and often lost __________.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Emma는 인내심이 부족하여 자주 집중력(focus)을 잃었습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ focus(집중력): lost focus = 집중력을 잃다
❌ ① interest: 비슷하지만 focus가 원문
❌ ② hope: 맥락과 다름
❌ ④ friends: 맥락과 무관
det.tip: lost focus = 집중력을 잃다. patience(인내심) 부족의 직접적 결과

questions.passage: Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading to improve her ability to sound out words. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some one-on-one reading instruction in addition to the small-group time. In those one-on-one meetings, Sandy let Emma select a book from a handful of books that were at her reading level. Then Sandy would read a paragraph out loud and have Emma read one. They would continue to __________ back and forth.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Sandy와 Emma는 번갈아 가며 교대(swap)하며 읽기를 계속했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② swap(교대하다): 번갈아 가며 읽기
❌ ① compete(경쟁): 교육이지 경쟁이 아님
❌ ③ argue(논쟁): 맥락과 무관
❌ ④ jump(뛰다): 맥락과 무관
det.tip: swap back and forth = 번갈아 교대하다. 교사→학생→교사 순서로 읽기

questions.passage: Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. Every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level. Emma was in one of Sandy's afternoon reading groups, and she was not improving. She lacked patience and often lost focus, at which point she became disruptive, primarily to amuse herself.
questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Emma는 인내심이 부족하고 집중력을 자주 잃었다.
Emma는 Sandy의 수업에서 빠르게 향상되고 있었다.
Emma는 학년 수준 이상의 읽기 능력을 보였다.

det.korean: ① 원문의 'lacked patience and often lost focus'와 일치합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 인내심 부족 + 집중력 상실: 원문과 일치
❌ ② 향상되지 않음(not improving)
❌ ③ 초등학교 교사
❌ ④ 학년 이하(below grade level)
det.tip: 핵심 사실 확인: lacked patience + lost focus

questions.passage: That evening after school, Sandy reflected on what Emma had said. Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some one-on-one reading instruction in addition to the small-group time. In those meetings, Sandy let Emma select a book from a handful of books that were at her reading level. Then Sandy would read a paragraph out loud and have Emma read one.
questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: Sandy는 방과 후 Emma에 대해 생각했다.
Sandy는 소그룹 시간 외에 일대일 교육을 추가했다.
Sandy는 Emma에게 읽기 수준에 맞는 책 중에서 고르게 했다.
Sandy가 책을 지정하고 Emma는 선택권이 없었다.

det.korean: ④ 원문에서 Sandy는 Emma에게 책을 선택하게(let Emma select) 했습니다. '선택권이 없었다'는 불일치입니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ 불일치: let Emma select(선택하게 함) ≠ 선택권 없음
✅ ① 일치: reflected(숙고)
✅ ② 일치: in addition to(추가로)
✅ ③ 일치: books at her reading level
det.tip: let + O + V: 자유롭게 선택하게 한 것이지 지정한 것이 아님

questions.passage: ①<u>Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level.</u> ②<u>The goal was to raise the reading level to help the school ascend from "academic emergency" status.</u> ③<u>Emma was improving rapidly in Sandy's reading group.</u> ④<u>Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading.</u>
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 원문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 문장은?

det.korean: ③ 원문에서 Emma는 향상되지 않고 있었습니다(was not improving). '빠르게 향상'은 반대입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 정상: 학년 이하 읽기 그룹
✅ ② 정상: 학업 비상 탈출 목표
❌ ③ improving rapidly → was not improving: 향상 안 됨
✅ ④ 정상: 연구 기반 전략
det.tip: not improving(향상 안 됨) vs improving rapidly(빠른 향상): 핵심 사실 변조

questions.passage: They would continue to swap back and forth. Slowly but surely, they saw improvement. Over time, they were able to increase the reading level of the books as Emma's ability to sound out words improved. Sandy also noticed that Emma came to reading group and started to make it through the entire lesson without becoming disruptive or feeling anxious.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"시간이 지나면서 Emma의 단어를 소리 내어 읽는 능력이 향상되면서 책의 읽기 __________ 을/를 높일 수 있었다."

det.korean: 원문 'increase the reading level of the books'에서 찾을 수 있습니다.
det.analysis: 패러프레이징: '읽기 수준' → 'reading level' → level
det.tip: reading level(읽기 수준): 책의 난이도를 나타내는 표현

questions.passage: Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. Every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level. The goal was to raise the reading level of the students. Sandy reflected on research and decided to take action. Her __________ (reflect) led her to implement one-on-one instruction for Emma.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: reflect(동사: 숙고하다) → reflection(명사: 숙고). 소유격 Her 뒤에 명사가 필요합니다.
det.analysis:
Her + __________ 구조에서 소유격 뒤 명사 필요 → reflection
reflect(동) → reflection(명) → reflective(형)
det.tip: reflect(숙고하다, 동) → reflection(숙고, 명): -ion 접미사로 명사화

questions.passage: Sandy reflected on what Emma had said. Sandy recalled research about reading improvement. The next day, Sandy took action. In those one-on-one meetings, __________ from a handful of books that were at her reading level.
questions.stem: 다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능) Sandy / a / book / let / select / Emma
questions.wa: Sandy let Emma select a book
accept: Sandy let Emma select a book
Sandy let Emma select a book.
sandy let emma select a book
sandy let emma select a book.

det.korean: Sandy는 Emma에게 책을 고르게 했습니다.
det.analysis:
Sandy(주어) + let(사역동사) + Emma(목적어) + select(원형부정사) + a book(목적어)
6단어 배열
det.tip: let + O + V(원형): 사역동사 let 뒤에는 동사원형

questions.stem: 다음 한국어 문장을 주어진 조건에 맞게 영작하시오. "그들은 향상을 보았다." 조건: They로 시작하고, saw와 improvement를 반드시 사용할 것. 4단어 이내로 쓸 것.

det.korean: 원문 'they saw improvement'를 영작합니다.
det.analysis: They(주어) + saw(동사) + improvement(목적어)
det.tip: saw improvement = 향상을 보다/확인하다

questions.stem: 다음 한국어 문장을 주어진 조건에 맞게 영작하시오. "Emma는 인내심이 부족했다." 조건: Emma로 시작하고, lacked와 patience를 반드시 사용할 것. 4단어 이내로 쓸 것.

det.korean: 원문 'She lacked patience'를 영작합니다.
det.analysis: Emma(주어) + lacked(동사) + patience(목적어)
det.tip: lacked patience = 인내심이 부족했다. lack = ~이 부족하다(타동사)

questions.passage: (A) Sandy worked with below-level readers. Emma lacked patience and was disruptive. (B) Sandy implemented one-on-one instruction, letting Emma choose books. (C) Slowly, Emma improved, stopped being disruptive, and gained confidence to read more.
questions.stem: 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 학급 규모가 학생 성취도에 미치는 영향
개별 맞춤 교육을 통한 읽기 부진 학생의 향상
교사의 연구 활동이 교육 정책에 미치는 영향

det.korean: 글의 핵심 주제는 개별 맞춤 교육(one-on-one instruction)을 통해 읽기 부진 학생이 향상된 것입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 개별 맞춤 교육 → 향상: 글 전체를 관통
❌ ① 표준화 시험: 본문과 무관
❌ ② 학급 규모: 부분적 요소
❌ ④ 교육 정책: 본문의 초점이 아님
det.tip: one-on-one instruction → improvement → confidence: 핵심 변화

questions.passage: (A) Emma lacked patience and was not improving in Sandy's reading group. (B) Sandy added one-on-one instruction based on research. (C) Emma's reading improved, she gained confidence, and wanted to read more.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은? 요약: 읽기 부진 학생 Emma에 대해 Sandy는 연구를 바탕으로 (A)을/를 추가 실시했고, 그 결과 Emma는 읽기 능력 향상과 함께 (B)을/를 얻었다.

det.korean: (A) 일대일 교육(one-on-one instruction) → (B) 자신감(confidence).
det.analysis:
✅ ① 일대일 교육 — 자신감: 핵심 흐름
❌ ② 그룹 활동: 추가된 것은 일대일
❌ ③ 성적: confidence(자신감)가 원문
❌ ④ 우정: 본문에 없음
det.tip: one-on-one instruction(일대일 교육) + confidence(자신감): 핵심 키워드

questions.passage: They would continue to swap back and forth. Slowly but surely, they saw improvement. Over time, they were able to increase the reading level of the books as Emma's ability to sound out words improved. Sandy also noticed that Emma came to reading group with her classmates and started to make it through the entire lesson without becoming disruptive or feeling anxious. More than anything, her newfound confidence made her want to try and read other books!
questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Emma의 읽기 수준은 전혀 향상되지 않았다.
Sandy는 Emma의 변화를 전혀 눈치채지 못했다.
Emma는 새로운 자신감으로 다른 책도 읽고 싶어했다.

det.korean: ④ 원문의 'newfound confidence made her want to try and read other books'와 일치합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 자신감 → 다른 책 읽기 욕구: 원문과 일치
❌ ① 향상됨(saw improvement)
❌ ② 더 이상 방해적이지 않음
❌ ③ Sandy가 눈치챔(noticed)
det.tip: newfound confidence(새로운 자신감): 향상의 결과이자 긍정적 변화의 핵심

questions.passage: Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. Every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level. The goal was to raise the reading level to help the school ascend from "academic emergency" status. Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading. Sandy let Emma select a book and they would swap reading paragraphs.
questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: Sandy는 학년 수준 이하의 학생들과 오후에 읽기 수업을 했다.
Sandy는 연구를 바탕으로 Emma가 읽는 단어 수를 줄여야 한다고 판단했다.

det.korean: ② Sandy는 연구를 바탕으로 단어 수를 늘려야(increase) 한다고 판단했지, '줄여야' 한다고 하지 않았습니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ② 불일치: increase(늘리다) ≠ 줄이다
✅ ① 일치: 오후 읽기 수업
✅ ③ 일치: let Emma select
✅ ④ 일치: gained confidence
det.tip: increase(늘리다) ↔ 줄이다: 핵심 동사 변조
